zh_title: 西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰现已抵达中东，林肯最后的护航终于回家
summary: 2026 年 11 月 15 日，西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 穿越印度洋。作为计划部署的一部分，该航母目前正在美国中央司令部责任区执行任务。美国海军照片 美国第三艘航空母舰及其护航舰现在位于中东。西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 于周日加入美国第五舰队。随着美国和伊朗之间的紧张局势持续存在，西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群的到来使美国在中东地区出现了三个航母打击群。周末，胡塞武装继续占领巴布埃尔附近地区。
content:
2026 年 11 月 15 日，西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 穿越印度洋。作为计划部署的一部分，该航母目前正在美国中央司令部责任区执行任务。美国海军照片 美国第三艘航空母舰及其护航舰现在位于中东。西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰 (CVN-71) 于周日加入美国第五舰队。随着美国和伊朗之间的紧张局势持续存在，西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群的到来使美国在中东地区出现了三个航母打击群。周末，胡塞武装继续对曼德海峡（连接亚丁湾与红海的战略要道）周围地区提出主权要求，而伊朗军队则声称他们周五袭击了位于巴林的美国雷达。美国中央司令部否认了社交媒体网站 X 上发布的有关伊斯兰革命卫队在巴林发射两架单向无人机并被击落的说法。 2026 年 11 月 16 日，美国水兵在尼米兹级航空母舰西奥多·罗斯福号 (CVN-71) 的飞行甲板上使用分配给第 8 直升机海上作战中队 (HSC) 的 MH-60S 海鹰进行飞行作业。西奥多·罗斯福号被部署到美国第五舰队作战区域，以支持中东的海上安全与稳定。美国海军照片 西奥多·罗斯福预计将接替 8 月底抵达中东的乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰 (CVN-73)。
虽然 GW 最终接替了亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰 (CVN-72)，但在安倍回国之前，这两艘航母都与乔治·H·W·布什号航空母舰 (CVN-77) 一起在中东执行任务大约一个月。目前还不清楚随着 TR 的到来，GW 将在该地区停留多久。布什、GW和TR在中东的存在是以美国航母在印太地区的存在为代价的。安倍在部署 321 天后启程回国，而其两艘护航舰——迈克尔·墨菲号 (DDG-112) 和斯普鲁恩斯号 (DDG-111)——则留在了后方。迈克尔·墨菲 (Michael Murphy) 在服役 346 天后于周四返回家中，而斯普鲁恩斯 (Spruance) 在服役 357 天后于周六返回家中。斯普鲁恩斯的部署时间比安倍多了 36 天，创下了驱逐舰部署的记录。阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号 (DDG-111) 于 2026 年 11 月 13 日返回圣地亚哥海军基地母港，结束了在美国第 3、第 7 和第 5 舰队作战区域为期 12 个月的战斗部署。美国海军照片 对于驱逐舰来说，长达近一年的部署是罕见的，它们通常会部署六到七个月。然而，海军警告水手和家属，随着海上服务试图满足政府的需求，部署将持续近一年。斯普鲁恩斯于 2025 年 11 月 21 日从加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥海军基地部署。
据海军发布的宣布该驱逐舰回归的消息称，该驱逐舰在第三、第五和第七舰队中服役，在整个部署过程中航行了超过 88,000 海里。 2026 年 11 月 13 日，海军水手和亲人欢迎阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号 (DDG-111) 返回其母港圣地亚哥海军基地，结束了在美国第三、第七和第五舰队行动区为期 12 个月的战斗部署。美国海军照片 斯普鲁恩斯号在部署期间参与了史诗狂怒行动，在此期间，作为持续海上封锁的一部分，驱逐舰禁用了货船 M/V Touska。虽然新闻稿称该舰发射了战斧导弹，但没有详细说明

【原文 English Original】
USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) transits the Indian Ocean, Nov. 15, 2026. The aircraft carrier is currently operating in the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility as part of a scheduled deployment. US Navy photo A third U.S. aircraft carrier and its escorts are now in the Middle East. USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) chopped into U.S. 5th Fleet on Sunday. The arrival of the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group makes three U.S. carrier strike groups in the Middle East, as tensions persist between the U.S. and Iran. Over the weekend, the Houthis continued to claim areas around the Bab el-Mandeb – the strategic chokepoint that connects the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea – while Iranian forces claim they attacked a U.S. radar in Bahrain on Friday. U.S. Central Command denied the claim posting on social media site X that the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps launched two one-way drones at Bahrain, which were shot down. U.S. sailors conduct flight operations with an MH-60S Sea Hawk assigned to Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron (HSC) 8 on the flight deck of Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71), Nov. 16, 2026. Theodore Roosevelt is deployed to the U.S. 5th Fleet area of operations to support maritime security and stability in the Middle East. US Navy photo Theodore Roosevelt is expected to relieve USS George Washington (CVN-73), which arrived in the Middle East toward the end of August . While GW ultimately relieved USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72), the two carriers both operated in the Middle East, along with USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77), for about a month before Abe headed home. It is unclear how long GW will stay in the area with TR’s arrival. Bush , GW and TR’s presence in the Middle East comes at the cost of the U.S. carrier presence in the Indo-Pacific region. While Abe headed home after 321 days on deployment, two of its escorts – USS Michael Murphy (DDG-112) and USS Spruance (DDG-111) – stayed behind. Michael Murphy returned home Thursday after 346 days deployed, while Spruance returned home on Saturday after 357 days deployed. Spruance’s deployment came in at 36 days more than Abe and set a record for destroyer deployments. Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance (DDG-111) returns to its home port of Naval Base San Diego, Nov. 13, 2026, concluding a 12-month combat deployment across the U.S. 3rd, 7th, and 5th fleet areas of operations. US Navy photo Nearly year-long deployments are rare for destroyers, which usually go out for six to seven months. However, the Navy has warned sailors and families to expect deployments that approach a year as the sea service attempts to keep up the needs of the administration. Spruance deployed on Nov. 21, 2025, from Naval Base San Diego, Calif. The destroyer operated in the 3rd, 5th and 7th fleets, traveling more than 88,000 nautical miles throughout its deployments, according to a Navy release announcing the destroyer’s return. U.S. Navy sailors and loved ones welcome Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance (DDG-111) as it returns to its home port of Naval Base San Diego, Nov. 13, 2026, concluding a 12-month combat deployment across the U.S. 3rd, 7th, and 5th fleet areas of operations. US Navy photo While deployed, Spruance was part of Operation Epic Fury, during which the destroyer disabled cargo vessel M/V Touska as part of the ongoing maritime blockade. While the release said the ship launched Tomahawk missiles, it did not go into details about the Iranian military targets. The destroyer did take out 12 drones and four anti-ship cruise missiles while in the Middle East, according to the Navy release. The “Raptors” of HSM-71 embarked on Spruance and flew 190 sorties during the deployment, reads the release. Spruance received the Presidential Unit Citation and Combat Action Ribbon following its role in Operation Epic Fury. The destroyer has been busy over the past two years. Before its most recent deployment, the ship was part of U.S. Northern Command’s southern border operations, leaving San Diego in March 2025. Prior to that, Spruance spent five months in the Middle East as part of the U.S. response to Houthi attacks on commercial shipping, coming home on Dec. 19, 2024.

title: Navy Weapons Division to Make Tomahawk Components in 2027
zh_title: 海军武器部门将于 2027 年生产战斧部件

content:
2026 年 2 月 28 日，阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰小弗兰克·E·彼得森号 (DDG-121) 在支持史诗狂怒行动的行动中发射战斧对地攻击导弹。美国海军照片 海军空战中心武器部门上周宣布，将于 2027 年 6 月开始制造战斧巡航导弹弹头的组件，届时一种新型炸药和推进剂混合器上线。 11 月 9 日，由 B&P Littleford 制造的新型 300 加仑搅拌机在加利福尼亚州中国湖推进实验室举行剪彩仪式。 NAWCD 在一份新闻稿中表示，一旦混合器上线，NAWCD 的弹头生产团队将努力在制造商雷神公司需要弹头之前准备好弹头，帮助确保连续、准时地将战斧交付给舰队。 8月，海军授予雷神公司一份价值229亿美元的合同，以加速战斧生产，目标是每年生产1000多枚导弹。在“史诗狂怒行动”之后，国防部一直在努力增加和加速导弹和弹药的生产，该行动导致弹药迅速消耗。五角大楼的努力还集中于扩大制造商和供应商的国防工业基础，建设产能和冗余。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，来宾聚集在大型混合湾，观看中国湖推进实验室剪彩后新型 300 加仑混合机的演示。
一旦在 2027 年 6 月左右上线，混合器将使海军空战中心武器部门的能量团队达到为舰队生产战斧弹头的生产率。美国海军照片推进和能量部门负责人瑞安·亨特在新闻稿中表示，更快的生产需要更大的弹头容量。中国湖的海军实验室和马里兰州海军水面作战中心印度司令部表示，他们可以进行弹头的生产工作。目前，雷神公司是战斧制造的主要承包商，而通用动力军械和战术系统公司负责加工弹头箱，而 L3Harris 则为其装载炸药。 9 月，L3Harris 和 NAWCWD 签署了一项多年的公私合作伙伴关系，以制造导弹部件。亨特说，根据该协议，NAWCWD 计划生产部分战斧弹头。一年前，当 NAWCD 能源团队从博物馆取出一个战斧弹头盒时，NAWCD 开始了拥有制造战斧弹头能力的过程。能源团队将炸药和火箭推进剂混合，并将其装入海军武器中。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，中国湖推进实验室大型混合舱中，新型 300 加仑行星混合器的叶片位于混合碗上方。该混合器将于 2027 年 6 月左右投入使用，将使海军空战中心武器部门的能量团队达到舰队战斧弹头的生产率。
美国海军照片 该团队清理了箱子并混合了 PBXN-107 炸药并填充了 WDU-36/B 弹头。测试、成像和 X 射线证实该团队正确填充了它。经过这一努力，今年秋天，同一个团队填充了七个首件战斧弹头，这是新生产商建造的第一批用于检查的装置。能量处理部门负责人赞恩·戈德特表示，一旦通过，它们将成为“中国湖”的第一批生产弹头。弹头由中国湖运行了数十年的 150 加仑混合器填充，新的混合器将取代它。在演示构建过程中，团队还发现

【原文 English Original】
Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG-121) fires a Tomahawk Land Attack Missile during operations in support of Operation Epic Fury, Feb. 28, 2026. US Navy photo The Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division will begin making a component for Tomahawk cruise missile warheads in June of 2027 when a new explosive and propellant mixer comes online, the division announced last week. A new 300 gallon mixer, built by B&P Littleford was inaugurated in a ribbon cutting ceremony on Nov. 9 at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory in California. Once the mixer is online, NAWCD’s warhead production team will work to have warheads ready before manufacturer Raytheon needs them, helping ensure continuous, on-time Tomahawk deliveries to the fleet, NAWCD said in a news release . In August, the Navy awarded Raytheon a $22.9 billion contract to accelerate Tomahawk production with a target of producing more than 1,000 missiles annually. The Department of Defense has been carrying out efforts to increase and accelerate productions of missiles and munitions following Operation Epic Fury, which has seen munitions rapidly expended. Pentagon efforts have also focused on expanding the defense industrial base of manufacturers and suppliers, building both capacity and redundancy. Guests gather in the large mix bay to watch a demonstration of a new 300-gallon mixer after its ribbon cutting at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, Nov. 9, 2026. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division’s energetics team reach production rate on Tomahawk warheads for the fleet. US Navy photo Faster production calls for more warhead capacity, said Ryan Hunter, head of the Propulsion and Energetics Division, in the release. Navy labs at China Lake and at Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division in Maryland said they could do the work to produce warheads. Currently, Raytheon is the prime contractor building Tomahawks while General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems machines the warhead cases and L3Harris loads them with explosives. In September, L3Harris and NAWCWD signed a multi-year public-private partnership to manufacture missile components. Under it, Hunter said, NAWCWD plans to produce a portion of the Tomahawk warheads. NAWCD began the process of having the capability to build Tomahawk warheads a year ago when the NAWCD energetics team pulled a Tomahawk warhead case out of a museum. The energetics team mixes explosives and rocket propellants and loads them into Navy weapons. The blades of a new 300-gallon planetary mixer rest above the mix bowl in the large mix bay at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, Nov. 9, 2026. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division’s energetics team reach production rate on Tomahawk warheads for the fleet. US Navy photo The team cleaned the case and mixed PBXN-107 explosive and filled the WDU-36/B warhead. Testing, imaging and X-rays confirmed the team filled it correctly. Following that effort, this fall, the same team filled seven first-article Tomahawk warheads, the first units a new producer builds for inspection. Once they pass, they become China Lake’s first production warheads, said Zane Goedert, head of the Energetics Processing Branch. The warhead was filled by a 150-gallon mixer China Lake has run for decades, which the new mixer will replace. During the demonstration build, the team also found the warhead specification needed a major update. Key parts and materials to address the issue can take up to a year to arrive, reads the NAWCD release. Patricia Hottowe, director of the Tomahawk Technical Project Office at NAWCWD, said in the release that the team spent much of the past year updating the specification and the approved supplier list. The Navy’s technical authority for the warhead must approve each new supplier and every future producer – Navy or industry – must build to that specification. NAWCWD also bought long-lead materials ahead of the multi-year contract, Hottowe said. A dozen new personnel have been hired to join the team, Goedert said. They will train under experienced technicians on safety, quality and procedures for about a year before working on their own. He added that loading the warhead is the easiest part while buying materials, bringing on people and getting answers are harder. Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Delbert D. Black (DDG-119) fires a Tomahawk Land Attack Missile (TLAM) in support of Operation Epic Fury, Feb. 28, 2026. US Navy photo The branch has filled warheads for the AGM-84H/K Stand-off Land Attack Missile-Expanded Response (SLAM-E) missile since the mid-1990s. Goedert said his team routinely turns one-of-a-kind prototypes around on short timelines. That experience allowed the team to move faster on Tomahawk. According to Hunter, the challenge comes from a system built for fixed multi-year schedules. Now that system must move faster on a shorter clock. China Lake’s facilities will be able to meet that challenge due to its layout. “Because our plant is dispersed and because we will be curing the warheads in a different area than we’re casting them, we’re able to do simultaneous processes that will get higher throughput,” said Hunter. The plant’s newest buildings grew out of a rebuild as the July 2019 earthquakes destroyed three energetics compounds in the Salt Wells area of the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, reads the release. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command broke ground on their replacements, known as the trio, in April of 2022. Goedert said the team designed the Motor Assembly Compound to cut handling. Large rocket motors risk damage each time crews move them after casting. The same layout will speed warhead work. Rear Adm. Eric Gardner, principal deputy for the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Munitions, spoke at the ribbon cutting and said the first-article warheads will lay the groundwork for China Lake to become an additional source of Tomahawk warhead production. “At PAE Munitions, we know that increasing weapons production takes more than contracts and funding,” Gardner said. “It takes people, infrastructure, materials, and strong partnerships across our Navy, our warfare centers and industry.”

summary: 俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动距离中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三边会议仅48小时。一段视频的屏幕截图显示，Tu-95MS 飞行员于 2026 年 1 月 21 日在日本海上空进行了一次飞行。照片由 Russian Defence Min 摄
content:
俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动距离中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三边会议仅48小时。一段视频的屏幕截图显示，2026 年 1 月 21 日，一架 Tu-95MS 的飞行员在前一次飞越日本海时。照片由俄罗斯国防部/阿纳多卢通过 Getty Images 拍摄 Anadolu 11 月 16 日至 17 日，Tu-95MS 轰炸机是几架俄罗斯军用飞机之一，在东北亚进行了广泛的演习，引发了三个地区政府的防空反应。据分析师 AviVector 称，共有五架涡轮螺旋桨动力轰炸机于 11 月 16 日从俄罗斯远东的乌克兰基地起飞。据报道，其中三架轰炸机在三架 Il-78M Midas 空中加油机的支援下，在日本海上空进行了大约 11 小时的训练飞行。据报道，一架 A-50U Mainstay 空中预警和控制飞机也在日本海上空飞行。与此同时，另外两架 Tu-95MS 继续向南驶向越南。今天，乌克兰空军基地的三架 Tu-95MS 和三架 Il-78M 在日本海上空进行了 11 小时的训练飞行。
一架 A-50U（RF-94268，红色 41）从符拉迪沃斯托克机场起飞，在日本海上空进行了一次侦察飞行。两架 Tu-95MS（RF-94202，红色 43；RF-94188，红色 44）… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) 11 月 17 日， 2026 日本和台湾均未正式确定参与各自空域事件的飞机类型。日本防卫省证实，11 月 17 日早些时候，两架据信是俄罗斯的飞机侵犯了福冈县冲之岛西北部的领空。第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分左右进入，于凌晨 4 点 10 分起飞。第二架飞机于凌晨 4 点 09 分左右进入，于 2026 年 4 月 10 日起飞。据日本防卫省称，凌晨 4 点 12 分，日本认为俄罗斯飞机于 11 月 17 日早些时候进入福冈附近冲之岛西北部的日本领空，第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分左右进入，第二架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分左右进入日本领空。 pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — 台湾安全监察站 (@TaiwanMonitor) 2026 年 11 月 17 日，日本防卫省称，日本航空自卫队 (JASDF) 派出西方防空部队的战斗机发出警告并采取其他措施。
穿过对马海峡后，飞机在与那国岛和台湾之间飞行，然后继续进入太平洋。 2026年11月17日，推测的俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本联合参谋部 该航线使飞机经过连接日本海、东海和西太平洋的几个具有重要战略意义的海上通道。据报道，俄罗斯飞机随后进入韩国防空识别区（KADIZ）。不过，据韩国国防部称，此次事件并未侵犯韩国领空。

【原文 English Original】
Russia has sent a pair of Tu-95MS Bear bombers for a rare visit to Vietnam. Unusually, the aircraft appear to have briefly intruded into Japanese airspace and passed through Taiwan’s Air Defense Identification Zone (ADIZ) along the way. The activity unfolded just 48 hours before Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and U.S. President Donald Trump are due to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China. A screen grab from a video shows the pilot of a Tu-95MS during a previous flight over the Sea of Japan on January 21, 2026. Photo by Russian Defense Ministry/Anadolu via Getty Images Anadolu The Tu-95MS bombers were among several Russian military aircraft conducting extensive maneuvers across Northeast Asia on November 16-17, prompting air defense responses from three regional governments. According to analyst AviVector , a total of five of the turboprop-powered bombers departed their home base of Ukrainka in Russia’s Far East on November 16. Three of the bombers reportedly conducted an approximately 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan, supported by three Il-78M Midas aerial refueling tankers. An A-50U Mainstay airborne early warning and control aircraft was also reported operating over the Sea of Japan. Meanwhile, the other two Tu-95MS continued south towards Vietnam. Today, three Tu-95MS and three Il-78M from Ukrainka Air Base conducted an 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan. An A-50U (RF-94268, 41 Red) from Vladivostok Airport conducted a reconnaissance flight over the Sea of Japan. Two Tu-95MS (RF-94202, 43 Red; RF-94188, 44… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) November 17, 2026 Neither Japan nor Taiwan officially identified the aircraft types involved in their respective airspace incidents. Japan’s Ministry of Defense confirmed that two separate aircraft believed to be Russian violated its territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, in Fukuoka Prefecture, early on November 17. The first aircraft entered at approximately 4:07 a.m. local time and departed at 4:10 a.m. A second aircraft entered at approximately 4:09 a.m. and departed at 4:12 a.m. Two aircraft Japan believes are Russian entered Japanese territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, off Fukuoka, early Nov. 17, per Japan's Ministry of Defense. The first was inside from about 4:07 to 4:10 a.m. local time and the second from about 4:09 to 4:12 a.m. The Japan… https://t.co/Sj7vHUFDMQ pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — Taiwan Security Monitor (台灣安全觀測站) (@TaiwanMonitor) November 17, 2026 The Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF) scrambled fighters from its Western Air Defense Force to issue warnings and take other measures, according to the country’s Ministry of Defense. Tokyo subsequently lodged what it described as a strong protest with Moscow over the incident. Japan also provided details of the aircraft’s subsequent route. After passing through the Tsushima Strait , the planes flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan before continuing into the Pacific Ocean. Flight path of the presumed Russian aircraft on November 17, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office The route placed the aircraft through several strategically important maritime approaches connecting the Sea of Japan , East China Sea , and western Pacific. The Russian aircraft then reportedly entered South Korea’s Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ). However, there was no violation of South Korean airspace, according to the South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff. Finally, Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense reported detecting two Russian military aircraft entering its ADIZ from the northeast. Overall, 2 sorties of Russian military aircraft were detected early this morning. The aircraft entered #Taiwan 's ADIZ from the northeast, flew through airspace east of Taiwan, and exited the ADIZ south of Taitung. The #ROCArmedForces have monitored the situation and responded… — 國防部 Ministry of National Defense, ROC(Taiwan) (@MoNDefense) November 17, 2026 The aircraft proceeded through airspace east of Taiwan before exiting south of Taitung. Taiwan’s armed forces monitored the activity and responded accordingly, the Ministry of National Defense said. The incident is notable because Taiwan’s defence ministry publicly identified the aircraft as Russian, rather than simply reporting unidentified military aircraft activity. As we have reported in the past , Chinese aircraft commonly fly into the southwestern part of Taiwan’s ADIZ. It is, however, worth noting that the ADIZ declared by Taiwan covers not only the entirety of the Strait but also portions of mainland China. In terms of Russian aircraft operating in Taiwan’s ADIZ, there are historical precedents, but such activity has been greatly reduced since the end of the Cold War. Taiwanese military analyst Chieh Chung told Focus Taiwan that Soviet and Russian military aircraft had previously operated inside Taiwan’s ADIZ in 1986 and January 2010. "The incident was not the first time Russian or former Soviet military aircraft had entered Taiwan's ADIZ, although such flights have become much less frequent since the end of the Cold War." https://t.co/TPUJL9hfp1 https://t.co/SDB6p3E3pD — Bryce C. Barros 白若詩 (@barros_bryce) November 17, 2026 The two remaining Tu-95MS aircraft continued south towards Vietnam and were subsequently reported at Da Nang on November 17. They were accompanied by a pair of Il-76MD Candid transports, one of which was a modernized -90A variant , to support the deployment. Tu-95MS strategic missile carriers RF-94202, RF-94188. Il-76MD, Da Nang Airport / "Danang 35K Feet". pic.twitter.com/22DaoD8PLP — Massimo Frantarelli (@MrFrantarelli) November 17, 2026 [Russie Vietnam] 2 Tu-95MS des forces aérospatiales russes sont arrivés à l'aéroport international de Da Nang (DAD/VVDN), au Vietnam. 2 avions de transport militaire IL-76 (MD et MD-90A) les accompagnaient. (c) AviaNews pic.twitter.com/4bWfFXFOik — La souris (@La_souris_DA) November 17, 2026 The flights took place against the backdrop of preparations for the November 19 meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin in China. The summit is set to be held on the sidelines of meetings of the  Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), which kick off tomorrow. Putin arrived in Shenzhen today. Trump has traveled first to the Philippines as part of a short tour of Asia before heading to China. Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen in the early hours of Nov. 18 to attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. ： @PDChina pic.twitter.com/5YotpjYY6R — Shenzhen Daily (@szdaily1) November 17, 2026 The proximity of the Russian operation to the Shenzhen meeting raises questions about the strategic signaling of the Russian flights, particularly as the three governments prepare to discuss nuclear arms control, regional security, and other major international issues. The meeting is particularly unusual given the different priorities each leader is bringing to the table . Trump has indicated that he wants to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals and addressing the war in Iran. The expiration of the New START treaty in February 2026 removed the remaining bilateral limits on U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear forces, adding urgency to the question of future arms-control arrangements. U.S. President Barack Obama, at left, and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, at right, shake hands after signing the New START treaty in 2010. Government of Russia Washington has tempered expectations of an immediate agreement, describing the gathering as an initial opportunity for the three nuclear powers to begin a conversation. Putin, meanwhile, is expected to seek discussion of Russia’s war against Ukraine and the possibility of a negotiated settlement. Moscow has signalled that Ukraine will remain a priority in its discussions with Washington. Beijing’s position is more cautious. China has resisted joining trilateral nuclear arms-control negotiations at this stage, arguing that its nuclear arsenal remains substantially smaller than those of the United States and Russia. Xi is also seeking to present China as a central diplomatic actor capable of facilitating dialogue between the other two powers. An apparent new field of Chinese intercontinental ballistic missile silos identified by Matt Korda and Hans Kristensen from the Federation of American Scientists (FAS) and located near the city of Hami in the eastern end of Xinjiang province, in the northwest of China. Kristensen/Korda/FAS 2021 The timing of the Russian aviation activity is therefore difficult to ignore. The operation demonstrated the geographic reach of Russian long-range aviation, with aircraft moving from Russia’s Far East through the approaches to Japan and Taiwan before continuing towards Vietnam. The Southeast Asian nation was a regular late Cold War operating location for Soviet naval Tu-95 Bear reconnaissance aircraft. Of course, as well as strategic signalling, flights of this kind provide valuable long-range training and intelligence collection, including assessment of regional air defense responses. The November 19 meeting may not produce an agreement on nuclear weapons or other major disputes. Still, the Russian flights underscore the fact that strategic stability in the Indo-Pacific also involves the security concerns of the regional states operating along the approaches to the western Pacific. title: Suspected Russian Aircraft Violated Japan’s Airspace, Says Defense Minister
zh_title: 防卫大臣称俄罗斯飞机疑似侵犯日本领空

content:
2026 年 11 月 12 日可疑俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本防卫大臣周二宣布，可疑俄罗斯飞机周四两次侵犯日本领空，促使战斗机紧急升空予以回应。日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎在周二的例行新闻发布会上表示，周四凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分，一架疑似俄罗斯飞机侵犯了东海冲之岛西北部的日本领空。随后，凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分，第二架疑似俄罗斯飞机侵犯同一地区的日本领空。飞机穿过对马海峡，在与那国岛和台湾之间飞行，然后进入菲律宾海。作为回应，日本航空自卫队西部防空司令部的日本航空自卫队战斗机紧急紧急升空。日本飞机向可疑的俄罗斯飞机发出了通知和警告。日本飞机无法看到俄罗斯飞机，也无法目视确认进入该空域的飞机类型。
会议记录显示，小泉纯一郎表示：“虽然很难明确说明俄罗斯飞机这次行动背后的意图或目的，但无论如何，防卫省和自卫队将继续高度关注俄罗斯的军事行动，并将采取一切可能措施，确保对领空侵犯保持警惕、监视和适当反应。”侵犯日本主权，也威胁日本安全。小泉表示，日本政府已通过外交渠道向俄罗斯政府提出抗议，要求类似事件不再重演。俄罗斯飞机周四进入日本、韩国和台湾的防空识别区（ADIZ）。防空识别区始于主权空域结束处，是一段确定的国际空域，为了国家安全利益，在其中检测和跟踪飞机。战斗机经常紧急起飞拦截和跟踪外国飞机，直到其离开防空识别区。虽然国际法不承认，但许多国家都设有防空识别区，因为领空距离一个国家的海岸线仅延伸 12 海里。这三个国家没有确认这架俄罗斯飞机的身份。
据当地航空观察员称，当天晚些时候，两架 Tu-95MS 轰炸机和两架 IL-76 运输机降落在越南岘港国际机场。岘港的一个社区社交媒体页面发布了轰炸机抵达的照片以及停在机场的四架俄罗斯飞机的视频。截至发稿时，俄罗斯和越南均已就越南境内出现轰炸机问题发表官方声明。日本军队于 2026 年 6 月 27 日拍摄到一架俄罗斯 Tu-95 轰炸机。日本联合参谋部照片 2015年，路透社报道称，美国已要求越南停止允许俄罗斯加油机使用金兰湾。据报道，这些加油机被用来为在关岛附近进行挑衅性飞行的俄罗斯轰炸机加油。俄罗斯轰炸机最后一次部署到东南亚是在 2017 年 12 月 5 日，当时两架 Tu-95MS 轰炸机和两架 Il-76 运输机降落在印度尼西亚比亚克岛。印尼空军表示，此次访问的目的是

【原文 English Original】
Flight path of the suspect Russian aircraft on Nov. 12, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office map Suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese territorial airspace twice on Thursdays, prompting fighter aircraft to be scrambled in response, Japan’s Defense Minister announced Tuesday. Between 4:07 and 4:10 a.m. on Thursday, one suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace northwest of Okinoshima, which lies in the East China Sea, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said in his regularly scheduled Tuesday press conference. Subsequently, between 4:09 and 4:12 a.m., a second suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace in the same area. The aircraft passed through the Tsushima Strait, flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan, and proceeded into the Philippine Sea. Japan Air Self-Defense Force fighter aircraft from the JASDF’s Western Air Defense Command were scrambled in response. The Japanese aircraft issued notifications and warnings to the suspected Russian aircraft. Japan’s aircraft were unable to see the Russian aircraft and visually confirm the type of aircraft that entered the airspace. “Whilst it is difficult to state with certainty the intent or purpose behind the Russian aircraft’s actions on this occasion, the Ministry of Defense and the Self-Defense Forces will, in any case, continue to monitor Russia’s military movements with the utmost attention and will take every possible measure to ensure vigilance, surveillance and appropriate responses to airspace violations,” said Koizumi, according to a transcript of the conference . Koizumi called the violation of Japan’s territorial airspace by Russian aircraft not only a serious infringement of Japan’s sovereignty but also a threat to Japan’s security. The Japanese government has lodged a protest with the Russian government through diplomatic channels and demanded that such incidents not be repeated, Koizumi said. The Russian aircraft entered the Air Defense Identification Zones (ADIZs) of Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Thursday. An ADIZ begins where sovereign airspace ends and is a defined stretch of international airspace in which aircraft are detected and tracked in the interest of national security. Fighter aircraft are often scrambled to intercept and shadow the foreign aircraft until it leaves the ADIZ. While not recognized under international law, a number of countries have ADIZs because territorial airspace extends just 12 nautical miles from a country’s coastline. The three countries did not identify the Russian aircraft. Two Tu-95MS bombers and two IL-76 transports landed at Da Nang International Airport, Vietnam, later that day, according to local aviation spotters. A Da Nang-based community social media page posted photos of the bombers arriving and videos of the four Russian aircraft parked at the airport. Russia nor Vietnam, as of publication, have issued official statements on the presence of the bombers in Vietnam. A Russian Tu-95 bomber photographed June 27, 2026, by Japanese forces. Japan Joint Staff Office photo In 2015, Reuters reported that the U.S. had requested Vietnam to stop allowing Russian tanker aircraft to use Cam Ranh Bay. The tankers were reportedly being used to refuel Russian bombers that conducted provocative flights near Guam. The last known Russian bomber deployment to Southeast Asia was on Dec. 5, 2017, when two Tu-95MS bombers and two Il-76 transports landed on Biak Island, Indonesia. The Indonesian Air Force said that the visit was for a navigation exercise. The Russian Defense Ministry said at the time that the bombers were refuelled in the air by Ilyushin Il-78 tankers over the Pacific Ocean. The last time a Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace was on Sept. 23, 2024 , when a Russian IL-38 Maritime Patrol Aircraft violated Japan’s territorial airspace three times north of Rebun Island. The Defense Minister Minoru Kihara said at the time that JASDF F-15J and F-35 Lightning II fighter aircraft were scrambled and discharged flares after the Russian aircraft appeared to have ignored the warnings issued. The incident was the first time Japan had released flares against foreign aircraft.

title: How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA
zh_title: 中国军队的作战准备情况如何？解放军之谜
summary: 中国军队的作战准备情况如何？解放军之谜 H.Seidl 星期二，11/17/2026 - 11:58 图片联盟/新华社 |高泽明评论 2026 年 11 月 17 日 阅读 4 分钟 中国军队的战斗准备如何？解放军的困惑 中国的武装部队比以往任何时候都更有能力，但也陷入混乱。安德鲁·斯科贝尔表示，无论中国军队有什么缺点，它在任何战争中都可能成为可怕的对手。 10月下旬中共二十届五中全会选举中央军事委员会副主席
content:
中国军队的作战准备情况如何？解放军之谜 H.Seidl 星期二，11/17/2026 - 11:58 图片联盟/新华社 |高泽明评论 2026 年 11 月 17 日 阅读 4 分钟 中国军队的战斗准备如何？解放军的困惑 中国的武装部队比以往任何时候都更有能力，但也陷入混乱。安德鲁·斯科贝尔表示，无论中国军队有什么缺点，它在任何战争中都可能成为可怕的对手。 10月下旬，中共二十届五中全会选举中央军委副主席张生民将军为中共政治局委员。党的领导层还确认了九月份中央军委高级将领被开除的消息，但没有任命任何继任者。这使得中国相当于美国军队参谋长联席会议的成员从通常的七人减少到只有两名成员：习近平担任文职主席，还有一名穿制服的军官张将军。中国人民解放军（PLA）被许多人认为是中华人民共和国（PRC）历史上最现代化、最有能力、最专业、装备最精良的军队。但它也正在经历自 20 世纪 60 年代毛泽东文化大革命以来的 6 年来最大的动荡。作为习近平反腐运动的一部分，自 2022 年以来，清洗行动已清除了 100 多名高级官员。
值得注意的是，这些被罢黜的将领中，有 50% 到 80% 是各级作战指挥官。 清洗运动震撼了国防机构 与此同时，中国的国防机构仍在承受四十年来最彻底的组织重组的冲击。 2016年启动的这次改革，不仅是为了增强解放军发动二十一世纪联合作战的能力，也是为了精简和集中军队，使其受中央军委主席习近平的直接指挥。这次重组被称为“中国的戈德华特-尼科尔斯”，以强调与美军在越战后时期强制各军种联合作战的举措的相似之处，这一举措花了几十年才完全实施。没有人知道习近平雄心勃勃的计划进展如何，因为中国人民解放军——包括空军、海军、陆军、火箭军和其他特种军种——尚未在21世纪发动战争，战争是对任何一支军队的严峻考验。现代化已将一支技术含量低、以轻步兵为中心、拥有陈旧空军和小型褐水海军的军队转变为一支机械化地面部队​​，拥有大量第四代和第五代战斗机空中力量，以及世界上最大的蓝水海军舰队。
此外，今天的解放军部队进行了更加真实的战斗训练，并且在过去二十年中参加了无数次（尽管大部分是小规模的）多国野战演习。中国武装部队在中国周边地区变得越来越积极主动和具有侵略性。在遥远的西部，地面部队的部署数量越来越多，在两国有争议的喜马拉雅边境沿线与印度军队偶尔发生小规模流血冲突。在南海，中国人民解放军海军、中国海警和海上民兵加大了对海军舰艇、海警快艇和渔船的骚扰力度，特别是菲律宾和越南的海军舰艇、海警快艇和渔船。在东海，中国海上力量已

How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA H.Seidl Tue, 11/17/2026 - 11:58 picture alliance / Xinhua News Agency | Gao Zeming Comment Nov 17, 2026 4 min read How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA The country’s armed forces are more capable than ever but in turmoil. Whatever the shortcomings of China's military, Andrew Scobell says it is likely to prove a formidable adversary in any war. The Fifth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) in late October elected the vice chair of the Central Military Commission (CMC), General Zhang Shengmin, to the CCP Politburo . The party leadership also confirmed the September expulsions of top generals from the CMC, but did not appoint any replacements. This left China’s rough equivalent to the US military’s Joint Chiefs of Staff with just two members, down from its usual seven: Xi Jinping as its civilian chair and one single uniformed officer, General Zhang.   The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is by many accounts the most modern, capable, professional and best equipped military in the history of the People’s Republic of China (PRC). But it is also enduring its greatest upheavals in six decades—since the turmoil of Mao Zedong’s Cultural Revolution in the 1960s. Purges have swept away more than 100 senior officers since 2022 as part of Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption crusade. Remarkably, between 50 and 80 percent of these ousted general officers have been operational commanders at various levels . Purges have rocked the defense establishment At the same time, China’s defense establishment is still absorbing the shock of the most thoroughgoing organizational restructuring in four decades. This revamping, launched in 2016, was not only intended to make the PLA more capable of waging twenty-first century joint warfare, but also to streamline and centralize it under the direct chain of command of CMC chairman Xi. This reorganization, dubbed “ China’s Goldwater-Nichols ” to underscore the parallels with the US military’s post-Vietnam War era initiative to compel separately stovepiped services to fight jointly—an effort that took decades to fully implement.  No one knows how well Xi’s ambitious initiative is faring, since the PLA – comprising the PLA Air Force, PLA Navy, PLA Ground Force, PLA Rocket Force, and other specialized services – has yet to wage war in the 21st century, warfighting being the acid test of any military. Modernization has transformed a low-tech, light infantry-centric military with an antiquated air force and a small brown-water navy into a mechanized ground force, with a sizeable airpower inventory of fourth-  and fifth-generation fighter jets, and the world’s largest blue-water naval fleet. Moreover, today’s PLA units engage in more realistic combat training and, for the past two decades, have participated in numerous, albeit largely small-scale, multinational field exercises. China’s armed forces have become increasingly activist and aggressive around the PRC’s periphery. In the far west, ground forces have deployed in ever greater numbers, engaging in occasional bloody small-scale clashes with India’s army along the two countries’ disputed Himalayan border . In the South China Sea , the PLA Navy, PRC Coast Guard and People’s Maritime Militia have stepped up harassment of naval ships, coast guard cutters and fishing boats, notably those of the Philippines and Vietnam. In the East China Sea , PRC maritime forces have conducted similar operations against Japanese and South Korean vessels. Perhaps most alarming is the dramatic escalation of so-called gray zone provocations around Taiwan. Modernization has strengthened the PLA  PLA formations are also operating further and further from China’s borders. Ground force units have served on United Nations peacekeeping missions around the world, while some air formations have also operated overseas. In 2026, the PLA acknowledged its first air installation outside of the PRC in Laos. Yet the most routinely deployed service overseas has been the PLA Navy. Its vessels have operated continuously in the Gulf of Aden since late 2008 and have been more active across the Western Pacific, Indian Ocean and Mediterranean, and even making appearances in the Atlantic, Arctic and Baltic seas. The PLA Navy has operated a support base in Djibouti on the Red Sea since 2017 and opened a naval base in Ream, Cambodia, in 2025.  But increased peacetime operational experience and tempo do not guarantee wartime successes. While PLA drills and deployments do not seem to have been impacted by the unprecedented waves of purges continuing across all echelons of China’s military, their effects could be different under actual combat conditions. The PLA has not fought a major war since China’s conflict with Vietnam in 1979. Muscular and intimidating shows of force around the PRC’s periphery and the periodic spectacle of smartly turned-out troops with gleaming military hardware on parade in Beijing are not incontrovertible proof of combat readiness. Nevertheless, as a former US defense chief famously remarked , “You go to war with the army you have.” In the event of conflict, the leaders of the PRC – just as much as those of other great powers – will have no choice but to send their militaries into battle irrespective of their condition or level of combat readiness – and their armed forces will salute and follow orders, executing operations as best they can. The PLA will remain something of a puzzle for a while, but it is likely to make a credible account of itself in any conflict. Its combat record over the decades has shown that it can fight effectively, absorb heavy casualties and adapt under fire. The views expressed in this piece are those of the author. title: Hong Kong private hospital apologises after doctor mistakenly removed patient’s ovaries during operation
zh_title: 香港私家医院因医生手术时错误摘除患者卵巢致歉
summary: 一名医生在手术期间错误地切除了一名女性的卵巢，一家私立医院向患者及其家人道歉。香港中文大学医学中心。照片：水浪/谷歌地图。香港中文大学（中大）医院行政总裁钟健丽周三在记者会上表示，涉事医生是一位经验丰富的合约妇产科医生。郑说，医生承认这起事件是由于手术当天与郑通电话时的失误造成的。医院没有透露这名患者的姓名
content:
一名医生在手术期间错误地切除了一名女性的卵巢，一家私立医院向患者及其家人道歉。香港中文大学医学中心。照片：水浪/谷歌地图。香港中文大学（中大）医院行政总裁钟健丽周三在记者会上表示，涉事医生是一位经验丰富的合约妇产科医生。郑说，医生承认这起事件是由于手术当天与郑通电话时的失误造成的。该医院没有透露该医生的姓名或任何纪律处分的细节，但表示将根据其人力资源政策实施纪律处分。首席执行官向患者、她的家人和公众致歉。他补充说，患者情况稳定，将获得免费的后续预约。卫生部周二在医疗哨点事件定期更新中表示，一名 45 岁女性患者的双侧卵巢在 9 月中旬被错误地、无意中切除。卫生部。资料图片：香港政府一站通。该患者被安排在一家私立医院接受腹腔镜子宫切除术和双侧输卵管切除术——切除全部或部分子宫，并切除双侧输卵管。
中大医院周二发布新闻稿称，手术前，手术同意书及原手术方案均明确注明保留双侧卵巢。声明称，“手术标本提取后，在对标本进行例行验证时，护士发现双侧卵巢被包括在内”。 “护士立即将这一差异通知了医生，因为这偏离了原来保留卵巢的手术计划。” “认知盲点” 医院的中文版声明因称医生在手术过程中存在“认知盲点”，因此“未能执行原定的保留卵巢手术方案”而招致批评。网上，有人留言称医院只是玩文字游戏，掩盖医疗事故。香港中文大学医院是一家新私立医院，于 2021 年开业。照片：Wai Ki Wong/Google 地图。钟周三表示，英文声明之后的中文声明翻译得很差。英国声明称，这名医生“情境意识暂时崩溃”。 “简单来说，涉案医生当时注意力不集中，”钟用粤语说。该私立医院表示，在9月12日发生医疗事故后，立即向患者及其家人“坦白”透露了情况，并表示诚挚的歉意。
它还在24小时内向卫生部通报了这一事件，并成立了根本原因分析小组进行全面调查。

【原文 English Original】
A private hospital has apologised to a patient and her family after a doctor mistakenly removed a woman’s ovaries during an operation. CUHK Medical Centre. Photo: 水浪/Google Maps. Chung Kin-lai, chief executive officer of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) Medical Centre, said during a press conference on Wednesday that the doctor involved is an experienced contract obstetrician and gynaecologist resident. The doctor admitted the incident was due to mistakes during a phone call with Chung on the day the operation was conducted, Chung said. The hospital did not disclose the name of the doctor or details of any disciplinary action, but said it would impose disciplinary actions in accordance with its human resources policies. The CEO sent apologies to the patient, her family and to the public. He added that the patient is in stable condition and will be provided free follow-up appointments. The Department of Health said on Tuesday in its regular update of medical sentinel events that a 45-year-old female patient’s bilateral ovaries were mistakenly and inadvertently removed in mid-September. The Department of Health. File photo: GovHK. The patient was scheduled for laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingectomy surgery – the removal of all or part of the uterus, and the removal of both fallopian tubes – in a private hospital. The CUHK Medical Centre said in a press release on Tuesday that prior to the operation, both the surgical consent form and the original surgical plan clearly specified the preservation of both ovaries. “After the surgical specimens were extracted, during the routine verification of the specimens, a nurse discovered that the bilateral ovaries were included,” the statement read. “The nurse immediately notified the doctor of this discrepancy, as it deviated from the original surgical plan to preserve the ovaries.” ‘Cognitive blindspot’ The hospital’s Chinese version of the statement draw criticism over its description that the doctor had “a cognitive blindspot” during the operation and therefore “failed to carry out the original surgical plan of preserving the ovaries.” Online, people left comments saying that the hospital was just playing with words to gloss over medical malpractice. CUHK Medical Centre, a new private hospital opened in 2021. Photo: Wai Ki Wong/Google Maps. Chung said on Wednesday that the Chinese statement, which followed the English one, was poorly translated. The English statement said the doctor had a “temporary collapse of his situational awareness.” “Put simply, the doctor involved had a lapse in concentration at the time,” Chung said in Cantonese. The private hospital said it “candidly disclosed” the situation to the patient and her family and offered sincere apologies immediately after the malpractice took place on September 12. It also informed the Department of Health about the incident within 24 hours and established a Root Cause Analysis Panel to conduct a comprehensive investigation.

title: Hong Kong whistleblower of student app scandal charged with doxxing
zh_title: 香港学生应用程序丑闻举报人被控人肉搜索
summary: 一名香港女子因质疑一名中学生获奖应用程序的合法性而引发学术诚信争议，她被指控人肉搜索。郑海莉.照片：Hailey Cheng，来自 Facebook。根据周三的法庭文件，海莉·程 (Hailey Cheng) 面临四项未经数据主体同意披露个人数据并造成特定伤害的指控。曾就读于香港城市大学、现就读于纽约哥伦比亚大学的郑女士当天在Threads上表示，该案已在法庭上提及，并已获准保释。一个
content:
一名香港女子因质疑一名中学生获奖应用程序的合法性而引发学术诚信争议，她被指控人肉搜索。郑海莉.照片：Hailey Cheng，来自 Facebook。根据周三的法庭文件，海莉·程 (Hailey Cheng) 面临四项未经数据主体同意披露个人数据并造成特定伤害的指控。曾就读于香港城市大学、现就读于纽约哥伦比亚大学的郑女士当天在Threads上表示，该案已在法庭上提及，并已获准保释。根据指控书，程被指控披露四名未透露姓名的人（X、Y、Z 和 A）的个人数据。据称，她这样做的目的是为了对这些人或其家人造成特定伤害，或者不顾后果地考虑是否会造成伤害。程被指控在未经“X”同意的情况下，披露了“X”的中英文全名、她的年龄、学校、学年、家庭关系、社交媒体资料、照片、居住区域、资格和行程。据称，她还披露了其他三人的个人信息，包括姓名、照片和家庭关系。 Y 的出生日期被泄露，Z 的住所被泄露，A 的社交媒体资料被泄露。
周三，郑在东区裁判法院出庭，在首席裁判官苏泽豪面前出庭，无需答辩。裁判官批准了辩方休庭寻求法律意见的请求，以及控方为受害者申请匿名令的申请。案件押后至12月23日审理。文件显示，郑以3,000港元现金保释。 2025 年 6 月，Cheng 担心 MediSafe（一款荣获多项奖项的药物处方应用程序）实际上并非由中学生 Clarisse Poon 制作，引发了病毒式的学术诚信丑闻。一家名为 AI Health Studio 的美国软件开发公司后来表示，该应用程序是受潘的母亲委托开发的，并且该应用程序未经其同意就提交给了比赛。早些时候被捕 这名大学生二月份在社交媒体上表示，她因举报事件而被捕。在八月份的一份声明中，她说她拒绝保释并被无条件释放。拒绝更新保释是指一个人拒绝接受延长保释期限并要求警方正式指控或释放他们的程序。警方稍后仍可以重新逮捕并指控嫌疑人。东部裁判法院。照片：何凯莉/HKFP。四月，程面临亲北京支持者要求被城大开除的呼吁。
香港编程协会 Facebook 群组的一名匿名成员当月发布了请愿书，敦促“香港庞大的蓝营”分享该请愿书。请愿书还表示，签名者将与警方、国家安全部门和中联办等当局联系，要求将她驱逐。据当时的当地媒体报道，在最初披露的三个月后，这家委托的软件公司证实了其参与，随后该学生的父母——著名肝病专家 Ronnie Poon 和 Roberta Pang——表示，他们的女儿将归还与 MediSafe 相关的所有奖项。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong woman who sparked a viral academic integrity controversy after questioning the legitimacy of a secondary student’s award-winning app has been charged with doxxing. Hailey Cheng. Photo: Hailey Cheng, via Facebook. Hailey Cheng faces four counts of disclosing personal data without a data subject’s consent causing specified harm, according to court documents dated Wednesday. Cheng, a former student at the City University of Hong Kong now admitted to Columbia University in New York, said on Threads the same day that the case had been mentioned in court and that she was granted bail . According to the charge sheet, Cheng was charged with disclosing personal data of four unnamed people referred to as X, Y, Z, and A. She allegedly did so with an intent to cause specified harm to those people or their family members, or being reckless as to whether the harm would be caused. Cheng was accused of disclosing the full English and Chinese names of “X,” her age, school, school year, family relationships, social media profiles, photos, living area, qualifications, and itinerary, without her consent. She also allegedly disclosed personal information of the other three people, including their names, photos, and family relationships. The person known as Y had her date of birth disclosed, while Z had his residence leaked, and the individual known as A had her social media profile disclosed. Cheng appeared before Chief Magistrate Victor So at the Eastern Magistrates’ Courts on Wednesday and was not required to enter a plea. The magistrate granted the defence’s request for an adjournment to seek legal advice and the prosecution’s application for an anonymity order for the victims. The case was adjourned to December 23. According to the document, Cheng was released on a HK$3,000 cash bail. In June 2025, Cheng raised concerns that MediSafe – a medication prescription app that won multiple awards – was not actually made by secondary school student Clarisse Poon, triggering a viral academic integrity scandal. A US-based software development company called AI Health Studio later said it was commissioned by Poon’s mother to build the app, and that the app was submitted to competitions without its consent. Earlier arrest The university student said on social media in February that she had been arrested in relation to the whistleblowing incident. In an August statement, she said that she refused bail and was released unconditionally. Refusing to renew bail is a procedure where a person declines to accept an extension of bail terms and requires the police to either formally charge or release them. The police can still re-arrest and charge the suspect later. Eastern Magistrates’ Courts. Photo: Kelly Ho/HKFP. In April, Cheng faced calls from pro-Beijing supporters to be expelled from CityU. An anonymous member of a Facebook group for the Hong Kong Programming Society posted the petition that month urging “Hong Kong’s vast blue camp” to share it. The petition also said that signatories would be in touch with the authorities, including the police, its National Security Department, and Beijing’s Liaison Office to demand her expulsion. Three months after the original revelation, the commissioned software company confirmed its involvement, following which the student’s parents – renowned liver disease specialist Ronnie Poon and Roberta Pang – said their daughter would return all the awards associated with MediSafe, according to local media reports at the time.

title: Hong Kong gov’t seeks HK$19.8 billion from legislature to fund early Ngau Tam Mei development
zh_title: 香港政府向立法机关寻求198亿港元资助牛潭尾早期开发
summary: 香港政府正在寻求立法会批准为牛潭尾早期开发阶段提供 198 亿港元的资金，牛潭尾是庞大的北方都会项目的一个主要区域。 2026 年 10 月 30 日，一幅横幅展示了牛潭尾的新开发区，新田大学城的一个校园区将坐落于此。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。发展局及土木工程拓展署在周二向立法会提交的文件中估计牛潭尾新D区的工地平整及基础设施工程
content:
香港政府正在寻求立法会批准为牛潭尾早期开发阶段提供 198 亿港元的资金，牛潭尾是庞大的北方都会项目的一个主要区域。 2026 年 10 月 30 日，一幅横幅展示了牛潭尾的新开发区，新田大学城的一个校园区将坐落于此。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。发展局及土木工程拓展署在周二向立法会提交的文件中估计，牛潭尾新发展区的工地平整及基础设施工程将耗资约198亿港元。根据该部门的预测，该地区占地约 130 公顷，将创造约 26,000 个就业岗位，并容纳 35,400 至 38,500 人。新田大学城是北部都会项目规划的三个高等教育集群之一，位于牛潭尾，占地约52公顷。该地区的五公顷土地已预留给香港科技大学管理的香港第三所医学院。政府表示，医学院周围约10公顷的土地将被开发为综合医院，以支持研究并为未来的北方都市居民提供服务。
牛潭尾开发区约一半（66公顷）是私人土地，政府估计大约有1,300户家庭和120家企业需要被驱逐，才能为该项目让路。油潭尾村入口，2025年1月25日。该村庄位于牛潭尾新发展区内，村民将从明年开始被驱逐。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。政府称，该项目将影响约5.7公顷农田、4.1公顷鱼塘和1个养鸡场。工地平整和基础设施工程预计将于 2034 年基本完成，居民最早可于 2033 年搬入。当局计划建设政府和社区设施以及休闲区，但尚未明确时间表。 2021 年宣布的北方都会项目计划将约 300 平方公里（约占城市面积的三分之一）改造成香港与深圳边境的创新和技术中心。另请参阅：科技城到大学城：为什么香港北部都会区将重点从高科技转向高等教育牛潭尾新发展区位于北部都会区项目设想的核心“创新科技区”内，该区还将包括专业服务和物流中心以及旅游和保护设施。发展区内的油潭尾村的居民将于明年起被驱逐。

【原文 English Original】
The Hong Kong government is seeking the Legislative Council’s approval of HK$19.8 billion in funding for the early development phase in Ngau Tam Mei, a major area in the sprawling Northern Metropolis project. A banner shows the new development area in Ngau Tam Mei, where one of the campus areas of the San Tin University Town will be located, October 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In a paper submitted to the Legislative Council on Tuesday, the Development Bureau and the Civil Engineering and Development Department estimated that site formation and infrastructure works in the Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area would cost about HK$19.8 billion. The area, spanning about 130 hectares, will create around 26,000 jobs and house a population between 35,400 and 38,500 people, according to the department’s forecasts. The San Tin University Town, one of three higher education clusters planned in the Northern Metropolis project, will cover about 52 hectares in Ngau Tam Mei. Five hectares of that area has been reserved for the city’s third medical school, which will be run by the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. Around 10 hectares surrounding the medical school will be developed into a general hospital to support research and provide services for future Northern Metropolis residents, the government said. About half of the Ngau Tam Mei development area – 66 hectares – is private land, and the government estimates that roughly 1,300 households and 120 businesses need to be evicted to make way for the project. The entrance to Yau Tam Mei Tsuen, on January 25, 2025. The village sits within the Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area and villagers are set for eviction from next year. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The project will affect about 5.7 hectares of farmland, 4.1 hectares of fish pond, and one chicken farm, the government said. Site formation and infrastructure works is estimated to be largely completed by 2034, while residents can move in as early as 2033. Authorities plan to build government and community facilities and leisure areas, but have not yet specified a timeline. The Northern Metropolis project, announced in 2021, is set to transform about 300 square kilometres – roughly a third of the city’s territory – into an innovation and technology hub along Hong Kong’s border with Shenzhen. See also: Technopole to University Towns: Why Hong Kong’s Northern Metropolis shifted focus from hi-tech to higher ed The Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area sits within a core “innovation and technology zone” envisioned under the Northern Metropolis project, which will also encompass a professional services and logistics hub as well as tourism and conservation facilities. Residents of Yau Tam Mei Tsuen, a village within the development area, will be evicted from next year .

This is the third of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe.   The negative numbers began to cascade across European balance sheets as soon as China entered the World Trade Organization in late 2001.   But the cost-benefit calculations were not equal for all Europeans. Some nations, such as Germany, initially gained from high-value exports and joint ventures. Others, like Greece and Portugal, faced a surge of low-cost Chinese goods and strategic investments by entities linked to the Chinese state.  The Chinese economy was barely one-eighth the size of that of the European Economic Community before the People’s Republic embarked on its policy of “reform and opening up” at the Third Plenum of the Eleventh Central Committee in December 1978. By 2025, the relative economic weight of China and the European Union was almost equal. Together they account for about a third of world trade. In 1975, their bilateral trade was worth about €2bn ($2.2bn) annually; 50 years later, it was €2bn a day , according to figures compiled for the Institut Jacques Delors.   By any measure, it should have been a success story. But the two were not playing on the same field. State subsidies in China, ranging from concessionary land deals to direct financial aid and favorable local taxation, handed Chinese firms a competitive advantage which added to their low labor costs. A thicket of protectionist rules and non-tariff barriers to entry frustrated foreign enterprises and channeled investment into joint ventures tied, inevitably, to forced technology transfer.   The EU trade deficits with China climbed remorselessly, from €39.6bn in 2001 to peak at €397bn in 2022 after the Covid-19 pandemic, before settling above €350bn annually. New infrastructure accelerated the flow of exports. While Chinese goods had to be shipped or flown to the United States, they could be loaded onto trains to Europe, cutting the transit time from more than a month to less than two weeks, avoiding bottlenecks and crisis points. Traffic on the railway link multiplied almost tenfold in the last decade.  At the same time, China’s leaders redirected their own investments abroad from buying fixed assets, like ports and factories, into new plants built to get around tariffs on electric vehicles and similar items. The Communist Party encouraged rapid growth in research and development, no longer content to copy and to sell. It meant to originate and to own the value in new products.  China’s patent filings now dwarf those by the EU, its universities regularly outrank their European counterparts, and Chinese academics lead the world in scientific publications. In short, a juggernaut was coming for the workplaces and welfare systems of Europe. The response has been episodic and ineffective.  In 2003, the European Commission declined to recognize China as a market economy, prompting ire in Beijing. The next year, the two made a customs co-operation agreement and pursued “dialogues” on tricky subjects like intellectual property and industrial policy.   A decade later, the EU changed its anti-dumping regulations to stay compliant with its WTO obligations but still refused to define China’s economy as playing by market rules. By then, Xi Jinping was settled in power, having taken all the great offices of the Chinese system between 2012 and 2013. Xi encouraged engagement on big-picture issues like climate change, but his focus on exports and technology acquisition was relentless. Meanwhile, waves of repression inside China created political barriers, notably to a bilateral agreement on investment which foundered amid strident criticism in Europe of the human rights abuses against the Uyghur Muslim minority in the far west of China. Such protests were never likely to move the Chinese leader. They merely encouraged him to grow economic ties with Russia and countries in what China was soon calling the “Global South.” The Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, followed by EU economic sanctions, deepened the dependency between Moscow and Beijing.   Their bilateral trade almost doubled as Russian oil and gas fueled Chinese factories and Chinese-made electric cars poured into the Russian market.  European leaders found that the political climate turned hawkish; Europe found itself caught between trade wars, a new strain of assertiveness in Chinese politics and the search for a balance between co-operation and rivalry, both between China and the West and within the EU. The Chinese decision starting in April 2025 to restrict exports of rare earths, valuable minerals for manufacturing everything from catalytic exhausts to pharmaceuticals, in reprisal for President Donald Trump’s tariffs, shocked business and political elites.  The “second China shock” has hollowed out the German industrial belts, forcing Berlin to move closer to the French preference for tariffs and barriers. By some counts in the German media, the country is losing more than 10,000 industrial jobs a month, fueling support for the right-wing AFD party, while France is struggling with its public debts.  In October, the two nations submerged their differences to write to the European Commission, urging it to use the trade weapon against competitors who exploited state subsidies and undervalued currency to destroy their rivals. There is also talk of diversifying supply chains and a “buy Europe” policy. The letter did not name names, but everyone knew the target was China. The proposed “second strike” capacity aimed at imposing duties on countries that retaliate when the EU imposes trade measures is an escalatory step that has uncomfortable echoes of nuclear deterrence doctrine. In Beijing, the Ministry of Commerce is unsheathing its own weapons and already talks of countries harming themselves by “wrong steps.”   The scene is set for a showdown of some kind. It is a far cry from the hopes of 2001.  Michael Sheridan is a veteran British foreign correspondent and is the author of ‘ The Gate to China ’, an acclaimed history of Hong Kong, and ‘ The Red Emperor: Xi Jinping and His New China ’, which is published by Hachette Books and has been translated into a dozen languages, including Ukrainian, Polish, and Japanese.   Europe’s Edge  is CEPA’s online journal covering critical topics on the foreign policy docket across Europe and North America. content:
这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章中的第二部分。起初，必要性是欧洲商业与中华人民共和国之间伙伴关系之母。在瑞士商学院，电梯制造商辛德勒的例子仍然是一个主题研究。 1979年，这家瑞士公司成为早期与中国的合资伙伴，尽管它与怡和洋行（Jardine Matheson）有联系，怡和洋行是一家与19世纪鸦片贸易有关的香港贸易公司。原因是：中国出现了住房危机。它正在向天空扩展，因为不断增长的人口需要塔楼。该国缺乏尖端技术，不得不到国外采购。最终，这家瑞士公司战胜了日本和美国的竞争对手。政治起了一定作用。瑞士于1950年承认中华人民共和国，是一个中立国。如今，中国拥有庞大的国内电梯行业，并与芬兰通力公司和日本日立公司等建立了合资企业。中国也需要汽车。它与大众汽车达成协议，到 1983 年春天，大众帕萨特的一个版本（更名为桑塔纳）开始在道路上行驶。其棱角分明的风格成为私人交通革命的象征。这些汽车是由上海大众汽车公司（现称为上汽集团）与德国公司和当地投资者的合资企业生产的。如今，上汽集团已成为电动汽车和电池领域的领导者。
在航空领域，空中客车公司开创了合资制造的先河，比美国飞机制造商麦道公司的合资企业更长久，并为欧洲发动机和技术的盈利出口铺平了道路。尽管中国致力于建造自己的商业上可行的民用客机，但这些出口仍然强劲。这些故事体现了欧洲的乐观情绪，这种乐观情绪伴随着中国从 2001 年开始加入世界贸易组织 (WTO)，并推动了本世纪初的贸易交易和外国直接投资。正如香港驻日内瓦代表所说，这是“双赢”。紧张的早期迹象出现在专利和所有权纠纷中。中国官员经常将“技术转让”视为对双方都有利的好事。它成为在某些领域开展业务的条件。跨国公司的国家经理往往主要热衷于扩大在中国的业务，他们会向总部保证他们的中国合作伙伴是值得信赖的。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。

This is the second of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe. At first, necessity was the mother of partnership between European commerce and the People’s Republic of China. At Swiss business schools, the example of Schindler, the elevator maker, remains a keynote study. In 1979, the Swiss company became an early joint venture partner with China, even though it had ties with Jardine Matheson, the Hong Kong-based trading house associated with the opium trade of the 19 th century. The reason: China had a housing crisis. It was expanding skyward because a growing population required tower blocks. The country lacked sophisticated technology and had to shop abroad. Eventually, the Swiss firm won out over Japanese and American competitors. Politics played a part. Switzerland had recognized the People’s Republic in 1950, and it was a neutral power. Today China has a giant domestic elevator industry of its own plus joint ventures with, among others, Kone of Finland and Hitachi of Japan. China also needed cars. It made a deal with Volkswagen and by the spring of 1983 a version of the VW Passat, renamed the Santana, was plying the roads. Its angular style became a symbol of a revolution in private transport. The cars were manufactured by Shanghai Volkswagen Automotive, today known as SAIC, in a joint venture with the German firm and local investors. Today SAIC is a leader in the field of electric vehicles and batteries.   In aviation, Airbus pioneered joint venture manufacturing, outlasting a venture by the US plane maker McDonnell-Douglas and paving the way for profitable European exports of engines and technology, which remain strong despite China’s drive to build a commercially viable civil airliner of its own. These stories exemplified the optimism in Europe which accompanied China’s membership of the World Trade Organization (WTO) from 2001 and drove trade deals and foreign direct investment through the early years of this century. It was, as the Hong Kong representative in Geneva had said, “win-win.” The early signs of strain emerged in disputes over patents and ownership. Chinese officials regularly spoke of “technology transfer” as a good which would serve both sides. It became a condition of doing business in certain fields. Multinational country managers, often keen primarily to expand their footprint in China, would assure head offices that their Chinese partners could be trusted. Meanwhile, low-cost Chinese manufactured goods poured into European markets under the tariffs agreed on entry to the WTO. Initially confident of their negotiating power as a bloc, the Europeans refrained from resorting to rhetoric about trade wars or dumping. The Chinese export wave, known today as the China Shock, was seen by specialists as a transitional phenomenon that would eliminate itself through the magic of free trade. Today’s leader, Xi Jinping, watched from a critical vantage point as the manufacturing and export boom in China turned a pariah state into an economic powerhouse that had foreign governments, banks and corporations knocking on its door. His fortunes, indeed, advanced with the country’s renaissance. Xi’s career took off in the coastal province of Fujian, which stood at the forefront of China’s export zones. It received a flood of investment from Taiwan, whose manufacturers realized that instead of trying to sell goods into the Chinese market, they should make things cheaply in China to sell to others. This was the trick that turned the world economy inside out. At some point during this period, party elders decided to favor Xi Jinping as a rising official whose consciousness of the value of trade was matched by his cautious disposition. In China, the consensus remained that prosperity and peace were indivisible (which also lowered the risks of any adventure to seize Taiwan). When Xi moved up the hierarchy to vice president in 2008, he visited a slew of European nations as he worked to understand foreign countries and to grow into the top role. He, too, was being auditioned: he met Joe Biden, then also vice president. For all the courtship of Europe, it was the United States which mattered most to China. That is why the financial crisis in the West of 2008 dealt such a blow to Chinese reformers. It broke out in the American credit markets and then spread to Asia. The economic slowdown was the most serious problem the Chinese regime had faced in the new century. Exports collapsed by a fifth, foreign investment slowed, domestic consumption fell, and thousands of factories closed, leaving between 10 and 20 million workers jobless. The blow fell most heavily in the coastal export zones where Xi had made his name and the global trade experiment was at its height. The crisis almost consumed the administration of President Hu Jintao and Prime Minister Wen Jiabao. The technocrats rallied the central bank, raided currency reserves and threw the power of the state behind a $500bn stimulus package that poured funds into high-speed trains and urban infrastructure, reforming the tax system and doling out credit. It was the zenith of pragmatic managerialism in China, but the legacy would be more Communist Party control, a taste for intervention in markets and an iron determination on the part of Xi Jinping that China would never again be subject to the shocks of international capitalism. Facing down America and balancing Chinese economic interests with Europe would be his mission. 黄仁勋 Megaspeed 丑闻对欧洲意味着什么？乍一看，情况并不多：欧洲人将继续购买英伟达芯片。但仔细观察就会发现，连锁反应将对跨大西洋关系以及欧洲与北京日益紧张的关系产生影响。荷兰及其明星芯片制造商 ASML 看起来尤其容易受到影响。黄也许是华盛顿最有影响力的中国鸽派。他几乎单枪匹马地说服唐纳德·特朗普总统及其内阁采取宽松的方式执行拜登时代对英伟达芯片的出口管制，这激怒了两党鹰派。他的影响力减弱，再加上有关通过新加坡向中国非法走私芯片规模的新揭露，意味着鹰派再次得势。美国商务部已经采取行动，禁止中国人工智能公司使用海外数据中心。三项法案似乎将被纳入《国防授权法》，以进一步打击中国使用美国芯片。其中之一——MATCH法案——针对的是中国的芯片制造工具供应。荷兰公司 ASML 是这些工具的全球主要制造商。在美国制裁的威胁下，它将被迫遵守其美国竞争对手目前面临的相同限制。

What does the Jensen Huang Megaspeed scandal mean for Europe? At first glance, not much: Europeans will keep buying Nvidia chips. But a closer look shows that the ripple effects will have consequences for transatlantic relations and for Europe’s increasingly tense relationship with Beijing. The Netherlands and its star chip machine manufacturer, ASML, look particularly vulnerable. Huang was perhaps Washington’s most influential China dove. He almost single-handedly persuaded President Donald Trump and his cabinet to take a lax approach to enforcing Biden-era export controls on Nvidia chips, to the fury of hawks on both sides of the aisle. His diminished influence, coupled with fresh revelations around the extent of illegal chip smuggling to China via Singapore, means that the hawks once again have the wind in their sails. The Department of Commerce has already moved to  block  Chinese AI companies from using overseas data centers. Three bills look  set  to be rolled into the National Defense Authorization Act that would further crack down on China’s use of US chips.  One of them — the MATCH Act — takes aim at China’s supply of chipmaking tools. Dutch company ASML is the major global manufacturer of these tools. It would be forced to comply with the same restrictions currently faced by its US competitors, under threat of US sanctions.  European and Dutch diplomats, including the Dutch Royal Family, have already  lobbied  against the MATCH Act, which looked unlikely to pass into law — until the Megaspeed scandal broke. In effect, the Act would ban ASML from selling new chipmaking machines to China, which accounts for around a  fifth  of the company’s annual revenue, and from fulfilling its contractual obligations to service existing machines already in the country.  Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular Bandwidth emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. Even if the MATCH Act passes, the White House will have discretion over how aggressively the legislation is applied. President Trump has tried to shield Nvidia and maintain good relations with Chinese President Xi Jinping. That gives Washington leeway to decline to enforce its toughest provisions — but still leaves ASML vulnerable to shifting political priorities or a future, more hawkish administration. If the US ultimately forces ASML to cut off servicing to Chinese companies, the Netherlands — and Europe — could find themselves exposed to Chinese retaliation. When Beijing  imposed  export controls on rare earths in 2025 in response to US trade actions, it ensured European companies were also caught in the crossfire. Beijing would likely not hesitate to make an example out of the Netherlands in order to discourage other countries from allying too closely with Washington. The MATCH Act is being discussed just as Europe itself is in the middle of executing a major hawkish turn on China, driven by the latter’s industrial overcapacities and supply chain dominance. Whereas the EU was unwilling to take a strong stance on China during Trump’s first term — when administration officials pressed European countries to remove Huawei telecoms equipment — and under former President Joseph Biden, the bloc is now developing powerful new trade instruments directed against Beijing. Despite this shift, Europe’s China policy remains fundamentally defensive. European capitals do not share Washington’s interest in undermining China’s AI sector. In fact, the EU benefits from Chinese competition to closed-source US frontier labs. Europe’s telecoms incumbents are resisting ripping out Huawei from their networks,  arguing  that the exclusion of Chinese suppliers would be  costly  and leave them dependent on expensive local vendors. US China hawks should think twice before trying to strong-arm Europe into mirroring US China policy. Such a move would likely backfire by galvanizing anti-US and pro-China figures in Europe. There is a deal to be done. For their part, EU countries need to follow through on the tough talk and deliver on China de-risking, with concrete measures such as improving coordination and closing gaps in EU and national licensing of chipmaking components. If Washington sees Europe acting of its own accord, it can formally take the threat of sanctions off the table. In the end, controls that allies adopt through their own volition are likely to prove more durable than those imposed on them by ultimatum. content:
这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第一部分。 20世纪90年代，天安门广场的阴影笼罩了欧洲与中国的贸易关系。 1989年对抗议者的屠杀标志着独裁统治的回归，政治改革的希望破灭了。欧洲公司撤退，实施武器禁运，孤立“北京屠夫”的政治压力也越来越大。然而，到了这个十年末，中国胜利地加入了世界贸易组织（WTO），其经济正在快速增长，随着“全球化”这个新词成为每次企业峰会的议程，世界已经来到了门口。为了重建这一转变，历史学家必须首先确定其背后的政治人物。即使天安门上的鲜血被冲洗干净——当未来的国家主席习近平的妻子、歌手彭丽媛为戒严部队唱小夜曲时——许多中国领导人知道他们犯了一个可怕的错误。其中包括习近平的父亲、两次被清洗的退伍军人习仲勋，他公开赞扬镇压“反革命暴乱”的“明智”和“坚决”决定，但私下里对经济改革的挫折表示哀悼。习仲勋亲自执掌南方经济强国广东，在20世纪80年代把它变成了吸引外资的世界工厂。他是影响 1989 年后中国下一届领导人选择的造王者之一。
这两名新面孔是从沿海贸易大都市上海走上来的。江泽民是上海共产党的领导人，也是一名受过苏联训练的工程师，后来成为国家主席和党的领导人。然而，关键人物却是一位名叫朱镕基的市长，他是一位出生于1928年、头脑敏锐的技术官僚。他先后担任央行行长和总理。天安门事件发生时，两人曾监督和平结束中国商业首都的大规模抗议活动。上海没有发生大屠杀。相反，朱在电视上发出严厉警告，当局则部署警察和民兵慢慢平息示威活动。上海很快就恢复了商业秩序。欧洲公司是浦东新金融区的第一批投资者。两位领导人不顾党内左派的强烈反对，决心让中国向世界经济开放。他们的活动可以通过日内瓦世贸组织的档案来追踪，这是谈判的宝贵指南。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。

This is the first of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe. In the 1990s, the shadow of Tiananmen Square fell across Europe’s trade relations with China. The massacre of protesters in 1989 marked a return to dictatorship and wiped out hopes of political reform. European firms drew back, an arms embargo was imposed, and political pressure grew to isolate “the butchers of Beijing.” Yet by the end of the decade China had swept triumphantly into the World Trade Organisation (WTO), its economy was growing fast, and the world was at its door as a new word, “globalization,” set the agenda at every corporate summit. To reconstruct the turnaround, a historian must first identify the political personalities behind it. Even as the blood was hosed off Tiananmen — and while the future President Xi Jinping’s wife, the singer Peng Liyuan, serenaded the martial law troops — many Chinese leaders knew they had made a terrible blunder. They included Xi Jinping’s father, the twice-purged army veteran Xi Zhongxun, who paid homage in public to the “wise” and “resolute” decision to suppress “a counter-revolutionary riot” but in private mourned the setback to economic reform. Xi Zhongxun himself had taken charge of the southern powerhouse of Guangdong, turning it into a workshop for the world that drew in foreign investment through the 1980s. He was one of the kingmakers who influenced the choice of China’s next leaders after 1989. The new faces were two men who had stepped up from the coastal trading metropolis of Shanghai. Jiang Zemin, the Communist Party boss in Shanghai, a Soviet-trained engineer, became President and leader of the party. Yet the key figure turned out to be a dynamo called Zhu Rongji, the city’s mayor, a sharp-witted technocrat born in 1928. In succession, he became governor of the central bank and prime minister. The duo had overseen a peaceful end to mass protests in China’s commercial capital at the time of Tiananmen. There was no massacre in Shanghai. Instead, Zhu went on television to issue a grim warning, and the authorities deployed police and militia to quieten the demonstrations slowly. Shanghai was soon back in business. European companies were in the first wave of investors in the city’s new financial district of Pudong. Both leaders were determined to open China up to the world economy, defying vocal opposition from leftists in the party. Their campaign can be traced through the archives of the WTO in Geneva, an invaluable guide to the negotiations. Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. As early as 1986, China had applied to join the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), but the major trading powers had decided to transform the GATT into a new body that would govern services as well as trade from January 1, 1995. It was too soon for China to join the new World Trade Organization at its birth, but negotiations began in earnest. The EU formed a negotiating bloc in rounds of bilateral talks between China and all its partners, which the WTO would then orchestrate into a package. Accession was vital to China, as Zhu Rongji argued in party councils. In 1993, for example, the People’s Republic recorded a trade deficit of more than $12bn, due to the cost of imports for modernization. At the same time, China’s foreign trade had soared to $195bn from $20bn in 1978, the start of the “reform and open up” era. John Bond, the chairman of HSBC Holdings, heard Zhu speak and realized that the Communist cadre had posed a modern version of the famous “Needham Question” raised by the Cambridge polymath, Joseph Needham, of why modern science had enjoyed a meteoric rise in Europe but not in China. “How can 22% of the world’s population account for less than 4% of the world’s GNP?” Bond asked. The WTO documents show the intricacy and the scale of that challenge. The rewards were obvious. In the five years after 1990, Guangdong Province, the former fiefdom of Xi Jinping’s father, saw an expansion across key industries of 40% every 12 months, according to the official Statistical Yearbook for 1996. Formidable obstacles remained. Zhu Rongji fought battles in Beijing to push through a 1994 package of changes to banking, finance, taxation, investment, foreign exchange and foreign trade. The working party in Geneva met behind closed doors 21 times between March 1996 and September 2001. The Europeans pressed hard on intellectual property, copyright protection, patents, trademarks (matters of great concern to Germany), test data, trade secrets, government procurement, minority shareholder rights, and judicial remedies. The WTO working party report alone ran to almost 200 pages. In the end, Europe had a deal. The fate of China was put into American hands. Between September and December 2001, the Clinton administration waged cliff-edge negotiations with the Chinese that remain controversial to this day. A myth has grown that China was ushered into the WTO by vested interests pushing a globalization and free trade agenda. The record shows that China’s road to accession was, in fact, long, painstaking and hard-fought. The final agreement imposed harsher conditions on China than any other nation when its membership became formal on December 11, 2001. It ran to 1,500 pages and weighed 13 kg (29 lbs.). Zhu Rongji saw his country become the world’s second largest economy, the biggest exporter, and the world’s largest holder of foreign currency reserves. He died earlier this year. “It was win-win,’ said the Hong Kong representative in Geneva from 1994 to 2002, Stuart Harbinson. “That was the conventional wisdom.” Michael Sheridan is a veteran British foreign correspondent and is the author of ‘ The Gate to China ’, an acclaimed history of Hong Kong, and ‘ The Red Emperor: Xi Jinping and His New China ’, which is published by Hachette Books and has been translated into a dozen languages, including Ukrainian, Polish, and Japanese. title: Government tech debt is a national security risk
zh_title: 政府技术债务是国家安全风险
summary: 8 月，美国联邦调查局宣布发现并阻止了另一起由中国政府发起的针对美国关键基础设施的网络攻击，这是一系列攻击中的最新一起，其中包括 2025 年 PlugX 恶意软件事件、2024 年 Flax Typhoon 黑客事件和 2023 年 Volt Typhoon 行动。这些攻击的严重性和频率应该引起警惕，因为它们显示了美国的对手寻找我们敏感系统中任何可能的弱点进行利用的模式，并且在许多情况下共同合作来这样做。这些攻击通常针对联邦政府
content:
8 月，美国联邦调查局宣布发现并阻止了另一起由中国政府发起的针对美国关键基础设施的网络攻击，这是一系列攻击中的最新一起，其中包括 2025 年 PlugX 恶意软件事件、2024 年 Flax Typhoon 黑客事件和 2023 年 Volt Typhoon 行动。这些攻击的严重性和频率应该引起警惕，因为它们显示了美国的对手寻找我们敏感系统中任何可能的弱点进行利用的模式，并且在许多情况下共同合作来这样做。这些攻击通常针对联邦政府自己的网络，而且往往很成功。即将上任的众议院和参议院网络领导人需要快速评估和解决此漏洞。数学并不在政府一边。网络对手只需正确一次，而防御者必须在每个系统、程序和供应商中都是正确的。不幸的是，联邦政府承包和管理关键系统的方式使其网络防御者的工作变得更加困难。联邦系统往往是在数十年的时间里拼凑而成的，往往具有不可预测的预算、不断变化的任务和采购规则，这些规则有利于增量修复而不是真正的现代化。过时的技术通常很容易识别。这个问题更危险的方面是联邦管理工作的复杂性，确保解决这一挑战将是困难的。
在管理和预算办公室以及总务管理局的指导下，联邦机构通常同时运行三到四代系统——遗留数据库位于云环境下，托管服务提供商和内部团队各自接触不同的层，通常没有共享的连接图。安全性通常是在任务发生变化、平台扩展和新的合规性要求出现之后才添加的。根据 R Street Institute 2025 年的报告，联邦信息技术支出每年超过 1000 亿美元，其中多达 80% 专门用于运营和维护现有系统。政府每年花费 800 亿美元只是为了保护旧系统的安全，而对手则投资新技术和工艺来渗透它们。对手现在可以访问代理人工智能系统来自动化其侦察工作，加速对已知漏洞的利用，并在补丁周期完成之前遍历供应链。联邦网络和防御的分散使得外国对手更容易渗透系统，并带来重大的战略风险。联邦政府可能不具备在与中国或俄罗斯发生危机或突发事件时继续运作的网络弹性。
国会开始关注，但由于网络投资不像新型战斗机或导弹系统那么有形，而且分散在每个议院的数十个授权和拨款小组委员会中，因此它往往处于次要地位。国会应该将联邦技术现代化视为一项安全需要，就像对待传统国防部武器采购一样紧迫。各机构需要采购途径，以便在无需多年采购周期的情况下采用可信的安全技术。供应商合同应足够清晰地定义责任，以便在发生违规行为后，可以在数小时内而不是短时间内确定责任方

【原文 English Original】
In August, the Federal Bureau of Investigation announced that it detected and disrupted another Chinese state-sponsored cyberattack targeting U.S. critical infrastructure — the latest in a series that includes the 2025 PlugX malware incident, the 2024 Flax Typhoon hack and the 2023 Volt Typhoon operation. The severity and frequency of these attacks should raise alarms because they show a pattern of America’s adversaries looking for any possible weakness in our sensitive systems to exploit, and in many cases cooperating together to do so. These attacks are often aimed at the federal government’s own networks, and they are all too often successful. The incoming House and Senate cyber leaders will need to assess and address this vulnerability fast. The math isn’t on the government’s side. Cyber adversaries only have to be right once, whereas defenders must be right across every system, program and vendor. Unfortunately, the very way that the federal government contracts and manages critical systems makes the job of its cyber defenders much more difficult. Federal systems are often cobbled together over decades, often with unpredictable budgets, shifting missions and procurement rules that favor incremental fixes over true modernization. The outdated technology is often easy to identify. The more dangerous aspect of the problem is the complexity embedded in federal management efforts, ensuring that addressing the challenge will be hard. Under the guidance of the Office of Management and Budget and the General Services Administration, federal agencies routinely run three or four generations of systems simultaneously — legacy databases sitting beneath cloud environments, with managed service providers and internal teams each touching different layers, often without a shared map of what connects what. Security is often added later, after missions have changed, the platforms expanded, and new compliance requirements emerged. Federal information technology spending exceeds $100 billion annually, according to a 2025 R Street Institute report , with as much as 80 percent dedicated to operating and maintaining existing systems. The government spends this $80 billion a year simply to keep old systems secure while adversaries invest in new technologies and techniques to infiltrate them. Adversaries now have access to agentic AI systems to automate their reconnaissance efforts, accelerate exploitation of known vulnerabilities and move through supply chains before a patch cycle completes. The fragmentation of federal networks and defenses makes it easier for foreign adversaries to penetrate systems, and it poses a significant strategic risk. The federal government may not have the network resilience to continue to operate in a crisis or contingency with China or Russia. Congress is starting to pay attention, but because cyber investment is less tangible than a new fighter jet or missile system and is spread across dozens of authorization and appropriation subcommittees in each chamber, it often takes a back seat. Congress should treat federal technology modernization as a security imperative with the same urgency it has applied to traditional Defense Department weapons acquisition. Agencies need procurement pathways that allow trusted security technologies to be adopted without multiyear acquisition cycles. Vendor contracts should define accountability clearly enough that, after a breach, the party responsible can be identified in hours rather than weeks. Platform duplication should also be reduced where it expands the attack surface without adding operational capability. Weapons acquisition reform is focusing on delivering capabilities to warfighters faster and at lower cost. Federal cybersecurity infrastructure acquisition should be held to the same standard. Faster modernization would make government harder to penetrate and quicker to recover. Government tech debt is a strategic vulnerability, and our adversaries are already exploiting it.
